participants.note: objected to handling the race condition in BaseIndex and suggested moving logic to net_processing
argued that getcfheaders/getcfcheckpt must be handled as well and suggested pausing the peer instead of queueing out-of-order
supported addressing the race in net_processing but objected to modifying index internals when GetSummary suffices

claims.harm: Handling peer race conditions inside BaseIndex couples indexing code to P2P transport concerns and risks stalls in other callers
claims.quote: Reading through this, I don't think this should be handled on the index level.
claims.settled_by_quote: Added deferring of a response, we store the racing request in a PendingCFilterRequest struct in a Peer and then check it in SendMessages.

claims.harm: Touching index internals violates separation of concerns when GetSummary already exposes sufficient state
claims.quote: Races in net_processing shouldn't be the business of indexes, and GetSummary() should have enough info... so I'd prefer if the index code was not touched at all
claims.settled_by_quote: Removed IsRacing, now using GetSummary. No changes in GetSummary were required.

claims.harm: Handling only getcfilters leaves getcfheaders and getcfcheckpt unhandled, which are responsible for most disconnects in practice
claims.quote: Based on the logs in #29655 this seems backwards -- there were more disconnects for getcfheaders than getcfilters? So I think this ought to be handled for all the cases?
claims.settled_by_quote: Yes, all three cbf messages should be handled the same way.

support.reason: Compact filter calculations are slow enough that races occur occasionally even for peers not on high-bandwidth compact block relay, so the issue is worth handling
Agrees that handling racing compact filter requests in net_processing makes sense to prevent disconnects and avoid delaying getblocktxn responses

result.notes: All initial objections regarding index coupling and scope have been resolved. The author adopted ajtowns's peer-pausing approach across all three BIP 157 message types and benchmarked the overhead.
